summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), stage 5 chronic kidney disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, and type 2 diabetes was readmitted for bilateral leg swelling and severe hyponatremia (sodium 115) ten days after a prior heart failure exacerbation. The admission was triggered by 10 pounds of weight gain, likely due to excessive fluid intake and dietary salt. She was treated with intravenous furosemide, which improved her volume status, corrected her sodium safely, and resolved her dyspnea. Her diuretic was transitioned to oral torsemide 60 mg twice daily, and carvedilol was temporarily reduced due to hypotension. Her condition stabilized over 11 days, with normalization of sodium, improved renal function (creatinine 3.5, likely new baseline), and reduced edema. She was discharged home with services, on an intensified diuretic regimen, with instructions for daily weight monitoring, fluid and salt restriction, and close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Alcoholic fibrosis and sclerosis of liver
